implemented_requirements.requirement: All seven standard Tetromino shapes are included
Tetrominoes fall from the top of the board
implemented_requirements.evidence: spawn() sets self.y = 0 and tick() repeatedly moves the piece down.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can move pieces left and right before they land
implemented_requirements.evidence: root.bind('<Left>', ...) calls move(-1); root.bind('<Right>', ...) calls move(1).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can rotate pieces before they land
implemented_requirements.evidence: root.bind('<Up>', ...) calls rotate(), which uses rot(self.m) and collision checks.
lock() builds list 'full' of rows where all cells are occupied, deletes them and inserts empty rows.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring increases with line clears and drops
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.score += LINE_SCORES[len(full)] * self.level in lock(); soft_drop adds 1 point per cell; hard_drop adds 2 points per cell.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when no more pieces can be placed
implemented_requirements.evidence: spawn() sets self.over = True if collides(self.m, self.x, self.y) after a new piece is generated.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board updates after each move or drop
implemented_requirements.evidence: draw() is called at the end of move(), rotate(), soft_drop(), hard_drop(), and tick().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop speed increases as the game progresses
implemented_requirements.evidence: tick() computes delay = max(100, 800 - (self.level - 1) * 70); level rises with lines cleared.

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional Tetris game meeting all core requirements: all seven tetrominoes, falling logic, player controls (move, rotate, soft/hard drop), line clearing, scoring, game‑over detection, board redraws, and progressive speed increase. The program is self‑contained, uses only the standard library (tkinter) and appears ready to run, so the submission passes.
